rationale:
The Dawn branch of adapter_info() hardcoded the adapter identity: name was assembled as "Native Dawn Adapter (<backend>)", description mirrored it, and vendor was the literal "Dawn". It never read dawn_info.device, .vendor or .description, so the reported identity described the backend rather than the driver. The wgpu-native branch in the same file already read those fields with empty-value fallbacks, so this was a fix that had reached one of two parallel paths. It matters concretely: android_gpu_adapter_identity() feeds exactly these fields to the Android Vulkan driver blocklist, which therefore could never match a real driver.

The family is crossed by exactly one path. Of the three changed paths in this branch, core/render/src/gpu_surface_dawn.cpp is the only selector hit, matching core/render/** (and, being a *dawn* file, core/view/**/*dawn* does not apply since it is not under core/view). Control, run against the same selector list: test/test_gpu_surface.cpp matches none of the fifteen selectors (test/test_skia* does not cover it) and .github/vellum-change-events/20260916-dawn-adapter-identity.json matches none. So the crossing is one implementation file, not a sweep.

No design-import, packaging, template, release-workflow or installed-SDK-staging code changes. No Skia build wiring, no asset changes, no authority moves and no Vellum artifact changes. Registered as watch-only so the family's coverage stays honest about a render-backend implementation fix that crossed its selector.
tests: GpuSurface adapter_info reports the driver's own identity
